meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a call at 4:40, Hale, so we have twenty minutes. My son found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that?
I don't have time for this. The zero stands.
You asked for this meeting, Hale. On what basis does it stand, and was Owen heard before you entered it? If you have nothing to show me, I'm going to the principal's office when we're done here.
Sorry. That came out wrong. Let me show you what I actually have: the essay quotes a line that isn't in Hamlet, and his October 15 outline argued cowardice, which the essay never mentions.

Students misquote Shakespeare and change their arguments between an outline and a final draft all the time, Hale. Show me the line, and show me the outline with its date on it. I'm writing down October 15.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed in today's meeting. I still demand that Owen's zero be withdrawn, that I receive an apology for the mark being entered before anyone called me, and that nothing be placed on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski
cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Still at her opening position, having agreed to nothing, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and nothing on Owen's record; the fair outcome would have been a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, but the meeting ended before any evidence was actually put in front of her.
What moved her: Naming two specific, checkable points, a quotation that isn't in the play and a dated October outline arguing something the essay drops, made her stop attacking and ask to see the documents, because that's the kind of evidence she trusts.
What cost ground: Opening by saying you had no time and the zero stood, with no basis given, confirmed her belief that the school punishes first and explains later.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence never came near that night, since you only raised an outline dated October 15 and a misquoted line, nothing about late hours; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked who decided and why nobody called, own entering the zero before calling home in one sentence, then turn the screen and show her the outline and the play side by side right away.
